newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds fall before key data, dollar firmer.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds fall before key data, dollar firmer.

text.p: Stocks and bonds fell Wednesday as investors braced for the May jobs report due on Friday, while the dollar rose against major currencies amid lingering uncertainty over Europe's plan for a single currency.
Technology stocks led the decline in stocks. But in contrast to recent sessions, the market's weakness broadened well beyond the beleaguered tech sector.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 42.49 points to 7,269.66. In the broader market, declining issues edged gainers, 1,322 to 1,150, on volume of 466.7 million on the New York Stock Exchange.

PepsiCo Inc. became the latest in a string of companies to warn of disappointing earnings, and its stock fell 2-3/8 to 35-7/8. It was the second most active on the NYSE, with more than 8.6 million shares changing hands.

With several recent earnings warnings still reverbating on Wall Street, analysts said it was understandable that investors opted to back off from the market, particularly with the May jobs report due Friday.

"No one is going to want to be a hero in front of the employment number," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "This market has discounted an awful lot of good news and has no margin for error in earnings or the economy or interest rates."
Selling pressure weighed heaviest on the tech sector, the source of the highest profile earnings warnings.

Analysts said the market probably would stay in a relatively narrow range through Thursday. Friday's jobs report is the last monthly employment report ahead of the meeting of Federal Reserve policy-makers in early July. The central bank's policy-makers held rates steady at their last meeting in May after raising them a quarter point in late March in a bid to ward off inflation.
The 30-year Treasury fell 5/32, or $1.56 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.88 percent from 6.87 percent on Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
After touching 1.7340 German marks earlier, the dollar settled at 1.7290 marks, up from 1.7275 late on Tuesday. It also edged up to 116.27 yen from 116.05.
Coffee prices fell after Colombia said it would soon supply more coffee to world markets.
At the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee for July delivery fell 12.65 cents a pound to 251.55 cents.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, July soybeans fell the 30-cent daily limit to $8.30 a bushel after Minneapolis-based grain giant Cargill Inc. said it was importing Brazilian soybeans.
The sell-off in soybeans pressued corn prices, as did excellent growing weather in the Midwest for the young corn crop. July corn ended 6-1/4 cents a bushel lower at $2.71-1/4.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil prices fell for a second straight day. Crude oil for July delivery fell 21 cents to end at $20.12 a barrel.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index fell 0.7 of a point to 4,557.1. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average rose 48.40 points to 20,611.56.
